# Corpus Mining: Hanna Moog & Carol K. Anthony, *I Ching: The Oracle of the Cosmic Way* (2002)

Source: `/mnt/agents/upload/_OceanofPDF.com_I_Ching_The_Oracle_of_the_Cosmic_Way_-_Hanna_Moog.pdf` (724 PDF pp.; text-layer extraction clean). Printed page numbers are cited where given by in-text cross-references (e.g. "p. 23", "p. 531"); otherwise section names are cited. PDF pp. 695 ff. = Appendix 3 (consultation rules).

**Book's core project:** a "new I Ching" dictated/verified by "the Sage" (the living consciousness speaking through the oracle) via the authors' retrospective three-coin method; it claims to strip away "feudal"/Confucian and "human-centered" distortions. Key meta-claim: the "I" of I Ching means **transformation**, not change — "One could say that the 'Book of Transformation' has been hidden for millennia under the cover of 'The Book of Changes'" (Part I, "Transformation versus Changes").

---

## 1. SMALLEST FRAGMENTS (decomposition)

### 1.1 Line types
- Two primary lines: **light line** and **dark line**. Idiosyncratic decoding: "the light and dark lines that make up the trigrams and hexagrams represent the Cosmic Way: the light representing the invisible Cosmic Consciousness, and the dark representing Nature" (Part I, "Transformation versus Changes"). They also encode **Yes (light) / No (dark)** — the oracle's ur-vocabulary.
- Coin values: heads = 3 (Yes), tails = 2 (No). Throws sum to 6, 7, 8, 9; "The lines composed of all even or all odd numbers (values 6 or 9)… are called 'changing lines'" (App. 3, "How to Develop a Hexagram").
- **Changing lines are redefined**: they "contain the pertinent messages given by the Sage… The changing lines point to a problem or misunderstanding that needs to be addressed…; freeing yourself from the cause of the problem is the true meaning of a 'changing line'" (App. 3). **No second/resulting hexagram is cast** (explicit rule, see R5 below).

### 1.2 The 8 trigrams = the "Cosmic Family" of consciousness types
Moog's central idiosyncratic primitive: each trigram is a **kind of consciousness**; together they are the "Cosmic Family" (Part I, "The Eight Trigrams", ~pp. 16–18 [page uncertain]; trigram names recovered by OCR of the page graphics):

| Trigram | Moog's consciousness gloss |
|---|---|
| **Ch'ien** (Heaven) | "The aggregate consciousness of all consciousnesses and their relationships" (= the Cosmic Consciousness) |
| **K'un** (Earth) | "The aggregate consciousness of all feeling consciousnesses expressed in form (Nature), and their relationships" |
| **Kên** (Mountain) | "The feeling consciousness of the earth (minerals). Its primary characteristic is non-movement" |
| **Tui** (Lake) | "The reflective consciousness of still water. As a state of mind, it is necessary for the inspiration described under Chên to occur"; in Hex 58: still water = "liquidity and stillness of the mind that make insight possible" = Cosmic Principle of Joy |
| **Chên** (Thunder) | "The state of mind in which the Cosmic Consciousness and the individual thinking consciousness meet as inspiration, best described as 'mind flashes,' expressed as 'Aha!' in Hexagram 51, Shock" |
| **Sun** (Wind) | "The consciousness of inner truth, which is our memory of what Cosmic Harmony feels like" |
| **Li** (Fire) | "The intuitive mind and its true function… forming images based on inner truth, resulting in clarity" |
| **K'an** (Water) | "The thinking mind and its true function: to form words that are based on images initiated by feelings of inner truth"; Hex 29: "the trigram K'an… stands for the role of thinking" |

Generation rule stated: "The last three trigrams [Sun, Li, K'an] describe how feelings are converted first into images, and then into words."
She **explicitly rejects** traditional correspondences: feudal family members, animals, 8×3-hour time sections, cardinal directions, and even heaven/earth/water/fire/lake/thunder/mountain/wind analogies are called misleading; "we did not use these analogies at all" (Part I, "The Eight Trigrams"). Note: she keeps the feeling-analogies (shock↔thunder, non-movement↔mountain, danger↔water, light↔fire, penetration↔wind).

### 1.3 The hexagram as unit
- Hexagram = "a six-lined configuration that is the result of pairing two trigrams" (Part I).
- **62 of the 64 hexagrams each describe one "Cosmic Principle of Harmony"; Hexagram 1 refers to all these principles; Hexagram 2 refers to those relevant to Nature, including the laws of physics** (Part I, "The Sixty-Four Hexagrams", ~p. 20 [uncertain]).
- Hexagram names: "We have been guided by the Sage to use only a particular English translation of the Chinese names… In a few cases we have given new English names altogether" — e.g. 1 = **The Cosmic Consciousness**, 2 = **Nature**, 3 = **Making a New Beginning**, 18 = **Recognizing and Correcting the Causes of Decay**, 49 = **Renewal/Revolution/Ending Fate**, 52 = **Meditating**, 53 = **Developing the True Self**.
- Two name classes: hexagrams naming a Cosmic Principle (Increasing, Returning, Limitation, Holding Together) vs. those naming a *misunderstood* principle (Youthful Folly, The Abyss, Oppressing/Exhausting, Darkening of the Light).

### 1.4 Strata of each hexagram entry (Part II format)
1. Name (+ alternate names).
2. **The Judgment** (italic oracle saying) = "the main oracle saying… an extension, in metaphorical terms, of the Cosmic Principle which is the theme of that hexagram."
3. Commentary on the Judgment (Cosmic Principle vs. human-centered misunderstandings; often lists mistaken beliefs, spells, seed phrases).
4. **Line 1 … Line 6**: italic oracle saying + commentary. "These line texts address the six different sub-principles described by that particular hexagram" (Part I). **No place-rank semantics** (no 1=beginning/5=ruler doctrine) — lines are sub-principles, not positions. [negative result: searched "first line/bottom line/fifth line/ruling line/nuclear" — nothing systematic]
5. **The Image section is REMOVED entirely**: "We were led to remove altogether the section added by the Confucian school called The Image, because of its misrepresentation of how aspects of Nature relate to each other, since this was no more than a justification of the feudal mindset and its customs" (Part I, "The Eight Trigrams").

### 1.5 Idiosyncratic primitives (Moog's invented vocabulary)
- **The Sage** — "an alive, but invisible consciousness," the Cosmic Teacher speaking through the oracle; referred to as "it"; "neither a master nor a servant"; relates to the student "as an equal with his true self" (Part I, "The Sage that Speaks through the Oracle", ~p. 24).
- **Helpers** — "the helping aspects of the Cosmos"; named by function: Helper of Transformation ("the vehicle for crossing" the great water; owner of "the wagon for loading", Hex 14 line 2), Helper of Increase, Helper of Creativity, Cosmic Doctor, Cosmic Surgeon, Health Helpers, Cosmic Banker, Business Helpers, Helpers of Relationships, Helper of the Love Relationship, Cosmic Army, Helpers of Fate, Personal Helper ("given to the individual person to help him fulfill his destiny"; one referent of "the great man"). Helpers can be **blocked, imprisoned, demonized, or retreating** due to mistaken beliefs.
- **Cosmic Principles of Harmony** — the 62 hexagram principles; the three most basic **Cosmic Virtues**: Equality, Uniqueness, Modesty; the binding force = "mutual attraction between complementary aspects. Another name for this force is love"; plus Cosmic Evolution, Fate, Transformation.
- **inner Yes / inner No** — the basic psychic operators: "He then says an inner Yes to what is harmonious, and the inner No to what is discordant. By saying the inner No, he separates from what is discordant and draws to himself what is harmonious, thus bringing about transformation" (Part I, Standard Metaphors). "Saying the inner No is a Cosmic Principle having the Cosmic function to transform discordant situations by removing their disturbing components in the atomic realm" (App. 1, p. 531). Said **three times** ("No, No, No") with inner resolve.
- **ego** (individual + **collective ego**), **true self**, **inner truth** (resident memory of Cosmic Harmony, located "in every body cell"), **commonsense**.
- **parallel reality** / **demonic sphere of consciousness** — created by "the false use of language."
- **seed phrases and images**, **mistaken beliefs**, **half-truths**, **verbal logic** — language-borne pathogens; Confucius's "seeds" of good fortune/misfortune.
- **projections, spells, poison arrows** — "the different kinds of negative effects produced by mistaken ideas and beliefs" (Part I, "The Human Gift of Language"); guilt-spells; the spell of original guilt/sin.
- **deprogramming** — permanent deletion of seed phrases/images (vs. the temporary inner No); mini-meditations (water image, fire image, "cosmic vacuum cleaner", "shredder"); deprogramming on behalf of another.
- **Fate vs. Destiny**: "It uses the word Fate to mean adverse events which a person creates by harboring thoughts and ideas that are in conflict with the Cosmic Harmony. It uses the word Destiny to mean the successful fulfillment of one's uniqueness" (Part I, "Fate", ~p. 32). "Every violation of the harmony of the Cosmic Whole… creates a fate for its originator."
- **mind-flash** — the Sage's momentary communication (image or words); "liquid light" as the medium.
- **chi energy** — life force; light and dark = two complementary aspects of chi.
- **The Three-Minute Rule** — "the amount of time the ego can maintain its energy during a determined assault… it can only get its energy by stealing chi"; stand firm through three waves (App. 1, p. 538).
- **Centering** (2 steps: suspending disbelief; loading things onto the wagon of the Helper of Transformation), **Closing an Inner Connection**, **Retreating from Conflict**.
- **Cosmic Family** = "the entire invisible world of the Helpers, the Helpers of Nature, and our own personal Helpers, as well as all the aspects of the Cosmic Consciousness that exist in form" (Hex 37 commentary).
- Glossary (App. 2) of ~45 terms: Animal Nature, Burnout, Chance, Chaos, Character, Chi Energy, Collective Ego, Commonsense, Cosmos, Creator, Culprit, Death, Demonic Sphere of Consciousness, Drives, Duty, Ego, Expectation, Fate and Destiny, God, Good/Evil, Good Fortune, Group-We, Guilt, Half-Truths, Helpers, Hero, Instincts, Light and Dark, Loss, Misfortune, Projection, Psyche, Punishment, Sacrifice, Senses, Soul, Spirit, Spirituality, Success, Supernatural, Transformation, True Self, Verbal Logic, Walking Dead Person, Work.

## 2. RULES

**Consultation prerequisites (App. 3, "Preparing Yourself")**
- P1. Know you are addressing an alive consciousness (the Sage), activated by inwardly asking for help.
- P2. Sincere and modest attitude required.
- P3. Open mind; suspicion or inner conflict makes the Sage retreat; put aside "wanting, wondering, or worrying."
- P4. The answer may lie outside your question; use rtcm to clarify.
- P5. "The answer of the Sage will invariably be to this inner question," not necessarily the phrased one.
- P6. Daily-consult formula: "Please show me what I need to know for today."

**Casting rules (App. 3)**
- R1. Three coins; heads = 3, tails = 2; six throws; build the hexagram **from the bottom up** ("Imagine you are building a house, starting with laying the foundation").
- R2. Identify hexagram via lower/upper trigram key (inside back cover).
- R3. Reading order: (1) note the hexagram's **name** ("In rare cases the name contains the whole message"); (2) read **The Judgment** (main oracle message, metaphorical); (3) read the **changing lines** received; (4) attend to whatever draws particular attention (resonance).
- R4. Changing lines = the pertinent messages; read within the context of the hexagram's general theme.
- R5. **No second hexagram**: "we were advised by the Sage not to follow the tradition found in other I Ching books of developing a second hexagram by changing the lines… first, the Sage clearly prefers simplicity, and second, the rtcm enables you to thoroughly understand the hexagram and the changing lines."
- R6. If nothing resonates, "the hexagram may be referring to someone else with whom you are connected"; verify with rtcm.

**The Retrospective-Three-Coin Method (rtcm) — Moog's core invented protocol**
- T1. Heads = Yes, tails = No. 3 heads = definitive Yes; 2 heads = "basically Yes" ("yes, but not quite to the main point" or "keep going in this direction"); 2 tails = "basically No"; 3 tails = definitively No (plus other meanings).
- T2. Purpose: verify hypotheses about the meaning of metaphors after casting; "it is important to make sure that the ego is not in charge."
- T3. "The Sage… does not use the same parts of the oracle text each time to mean the same thing. The rtcm helps you determine the unique meaning of the moment."
- T4. Termination rule: ask "Do I need to go further?" / "Is this all I need to know now?"; if Yes, thank the Sage.
- T5. **The Sage never answers the same question twice**; re-asking (even rephrased) returns the *reverse* answer — a signal of the Sage's withdrawal. Keep a written record (shorthand ++, +++, – –, – – –).
- T6. Long string of No's = wrong track (not withdrawal); ask "Do I need another hexagram…?" → "Should I discontinue…?" → "Is the answer so simple that I am overlooking it?"
- T7. Only certain translations (e.g. Wilhelm) "contain the necessary metaphorical language which enables the Sage to speak."

**Shortcut method**: ask (via rtcm) whether any part of the main text/Judgment is relevant; go paragraph by paragraph; then the changing lines; if no paragraph indicated in a changing line, the message is in the line's italic oracle saying. Write down indicated paragraphs.

**Questioning protocol (guidelines)**: identify the subject first (self? family? friend? public person? group? a Cosmic Principle?); then time element (past/present/future/in process); then inner vs. outer situation; ego-attitudes toward the Sage must be corrected first (inner No + apology). Several changing lines in one hexagram "can refer to different people in the situation" or give "an overview over a situation."

**Interpretive grammar**
- G1. Judgment → (commentary) → Lines; **no Image stratum** (removed, anti-Confucian rule).
- G2. Success/misfortune are **not predictions**: "It is not to be taken as a prediction that something bad will happen regardless of what the person does; it is given as a warning to tell him that he needs to correct his thoughts or attitudes" (Part I, Standard Metaphors).
- G3. Four-step consultation process encoded in **Yüan Heng Li Chên** (Hex 1 Judgment; Part I, "The Purpose of Consulting the Oracle", p. 23): Step 1 put the matter to the Cosmic Consciousness (Yüan); Step 2 see the inner truth with clarity (Heng — mind-flash, "penetrating"); Step 3 discern harmonious vs. disharmonious, say inner Yes/inner No (Li); Step 4 result = stability and duration (Chên).
- G4. Definitions: "Success… is undertaking something in cooperation with the Helpers of the invisible world… Doing one's share… and then allowing it to be completed by the Helper of Transformation." "Good Fortune… refers to the array of blessings received from the Cosmos by the person who is modest in his attitude." "Misfortune is the result of a person's separation from his true nature, and thereby from the Cosmic Unity."
- G5. Rejected traditional interpretive systems: shape-reading (Hex 20 as tower, Hex 23 as collapsing house), trigram-relation speculation (Hex 11/12, 63/64), the 12 calendar/solstice hexagrams — all called inconsistent or false; light/dark are complementary aspects of chi, "not two separate forces that fight each other."

## 3. SYNTAX / STRATA — formulaic phrase inventory (valence)

Traditional formulas retained (Wilhelm-based) with Cosmic glosses (counts incl. commentary discussion):
| Phrase | Count | Valence | Moog's gloss |
|---|---|---|---|
| "It furthers one to see the great man" | 8 (+ "great man" 29) | + counsel | recognize/ask the Sage in one's own and the other's presence; "great man" can = one's Personal Helper |
| "It furthers one to cross the great water" | 6 (+ "great water" 40 total) | + (conditional) | bring thinking into harmony with the Cosmos before undertaking; great water = demonic sphere / fate / projected fears; "vehicle for crossing" = Helper of Transformation |
| "It does not further to cross the great water" | 2 (+ "It does not further…" 15) | − injunction | goal incorrect, or acting from power/guilt/false duty |
| "Perseverance furthers" | 9 (+ perseverance 81) | + conditional | always "the perseverance of a mare" = correct cooperation with Nature / sensitivity |
| "It furthers to be firm and correct" | formula | + | discern inner truth first, then inner Yes/No; don't act outwardly yet |
| "It furthers to have somewhere to go" | 6+1 | + | find the right source of help = consult the Sage; also = separate from ego demands |
| "It furthers one to undertake something" | 5 (+17 "undertake something") | + | "undertaking something" = ridding oneself of demonic elements (Hex 1 commentary) |
| "It furthers one to appoint Helpers" | 2 | + | appoint Helpers of the invisible world, not humans (Hex 3) |
| "Nothing furthers" | 7 | − | full stop valence |
| Success / "supreme success" | 256 / 18 | + | harmony with Cosmos, cooperation with Helpers, result has duration |
| Good fortune / "brings good fortune" | 380 / 53 | + | Cosmic largesse/blessings to the modest; not chance-luck |
| Misfortune | 326 | − (warning, not prediction) | separation from true nature; a fate; signals need for correction |
| No blame | 208 | neutral+ | blame can be "extinguished" by sincere correction |
| Remorse / "Remorse disappears" | 168 / 24 | − / resolving+ | |
| Humiliation | 76 | − | e.g. "Entangled folly brings humiliation" = fate running to burnout |
| "It is not I who seek the young fool…" (Hex 4 Judgment) | — | protocol formula | Sage's dignity/retreat rule; NOT a limit on asking frequency |
| "Youthful folly has success" | — | + | |

Moog-internal mantras (fixed technical phrases of her system): "saying the inner No" (516 hits), "inner Yes" (18), "seed phrase(s)" (146), "poison arrow(s)" (266), "spell(s)" (823), "projection(s)" (211), "deprogramming" (199), "harmony with the Cosmos" (91), "true self" (310), "the Sage" (1186), "Helper(s)" (874), "fate" (713), "ego" (2032), "mind-flash" (12), "rtcm" (throughout App. 1/3). Valence: inner Yes/No = transformative operators; spells/poison arrows/seed phrases = pathogenic tokens; Helpers/Sage = beneficent agents.

## 4. CORRESPONDENCE TABLES
- **Trigram ↔ consciousness-type table** (§1.2) — her only systematic correspondence; replaces the traditional direction/season/animal/element tables, which she explicitly repudiates.
- Light line ↔ Cosmic Consciousness ↔ Yes; dark line ↔ Nature ↔ No.
- Coin sides ↔ Yes/No: heads = Yes = 3; tails = No = 2.
- Hexagram ↔ Cosmic Principle of Harmony (62 mappings, given by the Part II names/commentaries).
- Metaphor ↔ concept mappings: great water ↔ demonic sphere/fate/fear; the mare ↔ Nature; "wagon for loading" ↔ Helper of Transformation; "man of bronze" ↔ external authority; dragons (Hex 1) ↔ "the collective ego and its accumulated ideas"; ribbon grass (Hex 11 line 1) ↔ mistaken ideas to be pulled up.

## 6. Load-bearing quotes
- "With the exception of the first two hexagrams, each of the 62 remaining hexagrams describes a Cosmic Principle of Harmony. Hexagram 1 refers to all these principles, while Hexagram 2 refers only to those which are relevant to Nature, including the laws of physics." (Part I)
- "We were led to remove altogether the section added by the Confucian school called The Image…" (Part I, Eight Trigrams)
- "we were advised by the Sage not to follow the tradition… of developing a second hexagram by changing the lines." (App. 3)
- "The Sage neither makes decisions for the person consulting it, nor predicts a predetermined future." (Part I, p. 23 area)
- "The Sage never answers the same question twice… the answer given will be the reverse of what it was formerly." (App. 3)
- "Success and misfortune… indicate whether or not a person's thoughts or actions are in harmony with the Cosmic Principles." (Part I, "Success and Misfortune", p. 31)
